claims.claim: The rule-based convergence detector can fire 'converged' on a polite-agreement collapse: it only requires round>=2, every agent's disagreed_with_peer empty, and each agent's agreed_with_peer covering the peer's claim_ids. There is no minimum-claim-count gate and the 'stalled' check fires only when ALL agents emit zero claims (line 261-262). So one agent emitting one trivial cited claim + the other listing that claim_id in agreed_with_peer with empty disagreed_with_peer returns 'converged' on round 2. The Plan #34 ledger gate only blocks this when there are unverified citations or lineage flags — neither fires when the agent emits one well-formed citation and no prior round exists for rename detection.

The verifier upgrades evidence_path from 'bare str' to 'file:line that resolves and is in bounds', but does NOT check that the snippet actually supports the claim. _verify_one_citation returns status='verified' as soon as _resolve_path finds the file and _extract_snippet returns lines in range; claim text is never compared to snippet. An agent that emits claim='X is correct' with evidence_path='deliberate.py:1-2' (a docstring) gets a 'verified' ledger row. The schema's required evidence_path is necessary-but-insufficient for falsifiability.

The deliberate.py docstring claims 'Shares chassis with the duet: TaskFamily registry (Plan #31)' but build_deliberation_workflow has no task_family parameter, no profile lookup, and instantiates the chassis Position directly. By contrast build_duet_workflow takes task_family='generic' and dispatches plan_review_schema/implement_review_schema per profile. Domains wanting a deliberation variant with extra Position fields must fork. Structural asymmetry: the docstring promises parity the implementation does not deliver.

Synthesis defaults to synthesis_model='claude-code/opus' (deliberate.py:779), which is exactly the model used as agent_b in DEFAULT_AGENT_PAIR. In a two-agent default run the 'tiebreaker' shares model family with one participant — distorting the residual_disagreements list. Cheap fix: require synthesis_model to differ from both participants' models, or supply a neutral third model by default.

_detect_silent_rename keys on the first 80 chars of claim text. Brittle in both directions: (a) two different claims sharing a templated opening get false-positively flagged; (b) a polite agent reworking the first 80 chars while keeping substance bypasses detection. The comment acknowledges the trailing-edit choice but not the symmetric leading-edit evasion.

The position prompt only embeds the peer's latest position and own prior — not the full history. Per-round prompt size is bounded, not linear. What DOES grow monotonically is verifier_ledger.json (verifier:604-606 appends per-citation entries every round, never compacts). First failure at max_rounds>5 is therefore ledger reinstantiation cost (deliberate.py:701-704) plus absence of per-round cost cap (max_budget is a single scalar, not divided by max_rounds). Fixing 'context bloat' is not the right next priority because there isn't any.

Duet is asymmetric (gated cycle, duet.py:797-825). Deliberation is symmetric (peer debate, deliberate.py:9-22). Neither pattern covers N peers + a non-peer arbiter with explicit terminate authority — what synthesis half-implements but does not enforce. Right partition: three patterns (gated cycle, peer debate, arbiter-debate). Current synthesis merges findings but does not gate.

Single highest-priority improvement: upgrade the verifier from 'file exists + line range in bounds' to claim-vs-snippet semantic-relevance verification — either a deterministic lexical-overlap floor or a small LLM-as-judge that scores each (claim, snippet) pair and emits a new ledger status 'citation_does_not_support_claim'. This closes b1 and b2 in one move because detect_convergence already refuses to fire 'converged' when has_unverified_in_round is true (deliberate.py:300-307). Strictly higher leverage than b3-b7 because all of those presuppose the chassis distinguishes 'cited' from 'supported by citation' — which today it does not.

open_questions: Does tests/test_workflow_schema_smoke.py actually parametrize the deliberation Position schema, or only the duet PlanReview/ImplementReview schemas? The test file I read only parametrizes PlanReview, ImplementReview, TwinUpdatePlanReview, TwinUpdateImplementReview.
Is verifier_ledger growth bounded per-run by initial_state (deliberate.py:847 sets verifier_ledger=[]) or does a checkpointer-resumed run replay the full ledger?
Is the synthesis narrative or the residual_disagreements list in signoff.json the authoritative human-facing artifact when verdict='productive_disagreement'?
reviewer_summary: Ranking by leverage: (1) b1+b2 polite-convergence via existence-only citation verification is the load-bearing failure; both collapse into one fix. (2) b3 deliberation/TaskFamily asymmetry is a structural docstring lie. (3) b4 synthesis-as-interested-party distorts the only durable productive_disagreement artifact. (4) b5 80-char-prefix rename detection is porous adversarially. (5) b6 max_rounds>5 fails at ledger growth and unenforced per-round budget, NOT context bloat — fixing context bloat would be wrong priority. (6) b7 missing arbiter-debate third pattern is future-work, not current bug. Single highest-priority improvement (b8): upgrade verifier from file-exists-and-in-range to claim-vs-snippet semantic-relevance with a new 'citation_does_not_support_claim' ledger status that detect_convergence already honors via has_unverified_in_round. This single change closes b1 and b2 — the two highest-severity weaknesses — without touching topology or schema.
